mandatory_prelaunch_gate.failure_policy: Abort before the first launch; retain zero launches; do not weaken a gate.

attempt_protocol.sequence: sequential attempts 1 then 2; never reuse attempt output as later input
attempt_protocol.fresh_copy: Copy the same exact committed candidate into a new RUNNER_TEMP attempt-N/live/iTunes Library.itl for each attempt.
attempt_protocol.isolated_profile: Create a temporary junction at the per-user Music/iTunes profile path to only that attempt live root; remove it after the process ends and require it absent before the next attempt.
attempt_protocol.permitted_pre_target_ui: Only the exact known audio-configuration warning may be dismissed; every other non-target modal fails closed.

expected_modal.required_text_meaning: The iTunes Library.itl file cannot be read because it was created by a newer version of iTunes.

normal_dismissal_and_exit: Require exactly one visible enabled OK/default dismiss control in the target modal and issue BM_CLICK.
Wait up to 12 seconds for product exit; if still running require exactly one main iTunes window, issue WM_CLOSE, and wait up to 30 seconds.
Require exit code 0, zero remaining iTunes processes, no forced termination, and a removed profile junction.

capture_policy.window_metadata: Retain bounded top-level and child HWND, class, text, control ID, enabled/visible state, PID, and timestamps in JSON.
capture_policy.screenshots: Do not capture desktop or window bitmaps; metadata is sufficient and minimizes unrelated desktop capture. Missing/ambiguous metadata is a failure, not permission for an ad-hoc screenshot.
capture_policy.file_evidence: Retain prelaunch, modal-time, and post-exit file facts plus bounded independent semantic summaries; retain no Apple executable, DLL, MUI, resource, Ghidra project, or raw decompiler dump.

fallback_and_cleanup.timeout_or_unexpected_modal: Classify the attempt failed, capture bounded metadata, force cleanup only if needed, and explicitly record that forced termination is not modal success.
fallback_and_cleanup.cleanup_failure: Abort before any remaining attempt; do not launch again until zero processes and profile removal are proven.

predeclared_outcome_classes.two_attempt_success: Both fresh-copy attempts observe the exact newer-version modal, normally dismiss/exit zero, preserve the exact candidate and semantics, create no fallback artifacts, and require no forced termination.
predeclared_outcome_classes.partial_or_single_modal: Failed bounded reproduction; retain both declared outcomes where cleanup permits; do not substitute a candidate.
predeclared_outcome_classes.timeout_or_main_window_only: Failed predeclared outcome; any forced cleanup is not a modal success.
predeclared_outcome_classes.invalid_library_or_other_modal: Different native outcome; preserve metadata and fail without reclassification as newer-version.
predeclared_outcome_classes.input_changed_or_native_save: Failed causal gate because the candidate did not remain the pinned input.
predeclared_outcome_classes.prelaunch_gate_failure: Zero launches and no attempts authorized.

claim_limits: A two-attempt result is repeated observation of one exact candidate on one exact executable, not independent experiments or universal compatibility.
A product modal does not admit a 12.12.10.1 writer profile, arbitrary editing, or close U-01.
No timeout, forced termination, static resource mapping, or post-hoc candidate can be counted as modal success.

prelaunch_correction.reason: The first wrapper invocation failed closed before subprocess.Popen because the mature Authenticode helper returns a command/output record. The wrapper now parses and validates Status, Subject, and the locked certificate thumbprint.
